summary.text: Scott Phillips is a Democratic delegate representing District 10 in the Maryland House of Delegates and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as an attorney, entrepreneur and public servant and said he chairs the Criminal Law Subcommittee and, as of 2026, the Legislative Black Caucus of Maryland.

paragraphs.text: N. Scott Phillips graduated from Woodlawn High School, earned a B.S. in accounting from Virginia Union University in 1983, and received a J.D. from the University of Maryland in 1989.

His career experience includes work as a project director and consultant with the MBDA Advanced Manufacturing Center, as managing member of N. Scott Phillips Legal and Business Consulting Services, and as federal and public sector director of Precision Task Group.
Phillips took office in the House of Delegates on January 11, 2023, and serves on the Judiciary Committee.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he was raised in Baltimore City and Baltimore County and was first elected in 2022.

He listed as accomplishments sponsoring legislation creating the Board of Public Works Transparency Dashboard and supporting a bill that raised the Small Business Reserve procurement goal from 15 percent to 20 percent.
He also said he helped pass legislation allowing victims of gun violence to bring civil actions against firearm manufacturers and dealers.
